Opened fake “Word doc” that was actually a .LNK — Bitdefender detected shellcode, cmd keeps flashing. Wipe Windows?

So, I got hit by what looks like a fake recruiter/job-description malware attempt.

Someone claiming to be from some logistics firm sent me a Google Form for a job opportunity. I downloaded a ZIP that was supposed to contain a Word job description.
After opening it, another file briefly appeared then disappeared, Command Prompt flashed open and closed then Bitdefender started detecting malicious activity cmd.exe kept appearing every few minutes, even after I disconnected from the internet Bitdefender showed that the “Word document” was actually:
Apex_Role_Information_Document0926.docx.LNK
It also detected Generic.ShellCode.Donut... and some alerts said the suspicious apps “have not been blocked.” I shut the laptop down mid-scan and haven’t turned it back on since. From another clean device I already: changed Google passwords, logged the infected laptop out of Google, changed social media passwords, revoked active sessions, and secured important accounts
The laptop runs Windows 11 Home. Important files are already backed up in the cloud.
My main question: would you consider this Windows install compromised enough to just wipe it and do a clean reinstall from USB?

Or is it worth first checking:
Task Scheduler
Autoruns
other persistence locations
I was also considering Tron Script, but I’m not sure it makes sense before understanding what actually ran.
Would also appreciate thoughts and advice on what to do and whether a clean Windows reinstall would be sufficient here.

My machine is Lenovo Legion 5 16IRX9 (Type 83DG)

4) What’s the best way to redact social media history, if I so choose?   For example, I have a decade+ history here - that’s a lot to manually do.  I’ve looked at Redact.dev, but I’m leery about giving them access.

5) Is there a way to improve phone safety in public.  I’ve read about fake cell towers, for example, that mimic real ones and grab your data.

6) What about credit card skimmers?  I always wiggle the readers at gas pumps and the like, but what about ones that can be used walking past people in a crowd.  How do I best protect vs that?  Or is that such a rare threat that it doesn’t warrant concern.

I don’t feel like I’m an idiot, but I feel outpaced - I use robust passwords and don’t click email links, I scan regularly, I don’t connect to public wifi, I don’t click browser ads or browse shady sites.  I just worry that’s simply not enough.  I’ve had data breaches (not my end, at the end of the company I was using) a few times, so I know I can’t put it all back in the box.
